title: Red with anger or feeling blue? The link between color and emotion, with Domicele Jonauskaite, PhD

sentences.en: Does your anger burn fiery red?
sentences.zh: 你的怒火会炽热如火吗？

sentences.en: When you're sad, do you say that you're feeling blue?
sentences.zh: 当你悲伤时，你会说自己感到忧郁吗？

sentences.en: Have you ever felt green with envy or purple with rage?
sentences.zh: 你曾感到过嫉妒得发绿或是气得发紫吗？

sentences.en: English speakers are familiar with these color metaphors, all of which rely on linking color with emotion.
sentences.zh: 英语使用者对这些颜色隐喻都很熟悉，它们都依赖于将颜色与情感联系起来。

sentences.en: But where do those links come from?
sentences.zh: 但这些联系是从何而来的呢？

sentences.en: Are they universal, or do different cultures have different color emotion associations?
sentences.zh: 它们是普遍存在的，还是不同的文化有不同的颜色情感联结？

sentences.en: And can colors actually make you feel calm or sad or angry?
sentences.zh: 颜色真的能让你感到平静、悲伤或愤怒吗？

sentences.en: Will painting the walls of your house blue help you feel calmer at home?
sentences.zh: 把家里的墙壁漆成蓝色能帮你在家里感到更平静吗？

sentences.en: Is there a reason that so many hospitals seem to be painted a particular shade of green?
sentences.zh: 为什么那么多医院似乎都刷成特定色调的绿色，这有什么原因吗？

sentences.en: And is there any relationship to the notion that green is associated with feeling sick to your stomach?
sentences.zh: 这与绿色让人联想到胃部不适的观念有什么关系吗？

sentences.en: Color psychologists are studying questions like these and others too.
sentences.zh: 色彩心理学家正在研究这些以及其他类似的问题。

sentences.en: For instance, do people's favorite colors tell us anything about their personality?
sentences.zh: 例如，人们最喜欢的颜色能告诉我们关于他们性格的什么信息吗？

sentences.en: Are there universal favorite colors?
sentences.zh: 是否存在大家普遍最喜欢的颜色？

sentences.en: Are there gender differences in how people experience or describe color?
sentences.zh: 人们在体验或描述颜色时是否存在性别差异？

sentences.en: Why do we associate pink with girls and blue with boys?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们把粉色和女孩联系在一起，而把蓝色和男孩联系在一起？

sentences.en: And more broadly, how does color affect human cognition and emotion?
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，颜色是如何影响人类的认知和情感的？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客

sentences.en: Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Domitsella Jonoskaita, a senior research fellow at the
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是多米切拉·约诺斯凯塔博士，她是奥地利维也纳大学的高级研究员。

sentences.en: University of Vienna in Austria.
sentences.zh: 维也纳大学的高级研究员。

sentences.en: She is an experimental color psychologist who studies the links between color and emotion and cognition across cultures and individuals.
sentences.zh: 她是一名实验色彩心理学家，研究不同文化和个体中颜色与情感、认知之间的联系。

sentences.en: She's also interested in the role of color in aesthetics and art.
sentences.zh: 她也对色彩在美学和艺术中的作用感兴趣。

sentences.en: In her work, she aims to use rigorous research to validate or debunk myths in color psychology.
sentences.zh: 在她的工作中，她旨在通过严谨的研究来验证或打破色彩心理学中的迷思。

sentences.en: She has authored dozens of scientific articles and also writes a blog for the general public called Color Psychology.
sentences.zh: 她撰写了数十篇科学文章，还为大众写了一个名为《色彩心理学》的博客。

sentences.en: Dr. Jonas
sentences.zh: 约纳

sentences.en: Skaite, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 斯凯塔博士，谢谢你今天作客。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Are color associations universal?
sentences.zh: 颜色联结是普遍存在的吗？

sentences.en: Do people around the world associate the same colors with the same emotion or does it vary by country and culture?
sentences.zh: 世界各地的人们是否将相同的颜色与相同的情感联系起来，还是因国家和文化而异？

sentences.en: You've done some research in this area.
sentences.zh: 你在这个领域做过一些研究。

sentences.en: Tell us what you found.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲你的发现。

sentences.en: So we actually wanted the same thing are the links between colors and emotions universal so we started the
sentences.zh: 所以我们其实想弄清楚同一件事：颜色和情感之间的联系是普遍存在的吗？因此我们启动了

sentences.en: international color emotion association survey currently running in 80 countries and we have it
sentences.zh: 国际色彩情感联结调查，目前在80个国家进行，并且我们有

sentences.en: in 46 languages which sounds like an amazing amazingly big work to do and we managed to collect
sentences.zh: 46种语言版本。这听起来是一项极其庞大的工作，我们成功收集了

sentences.en: data from over 15 000 participants and now we kind of have an answer to this question and the answer
sentences.zh: 来自15000多名参与者的数据，现在我们算是有了一个答案，答案是

sentences.en: is yes the links between colors and emotions are universal so wherever you go in the world you will
sentences.zh: 是的，颜色和情感之间的联系是普遍存在的。所以无论你走到世界的哪个角落，你都会

sentences.en: find that people associate red with anger and love yellow with joy black with sadness and so on and
sentences.zh: 发现人们将红色与愤怒和爱联系在一起，黄色与喜悦联系在一起，黑色与悲伤联系在一起，等等。

sentences.en: of course there are also some more culture specific associations for example we know that
sentences.zh: 当然，也有一些更具文化特异性的联结，例如我们知道

sentences.en: red is a color of good luck in china so on top of these universal associations they also have
sentences.zh: 红色在中国是好运的颜色，所以在这些普遍联结之外，他们也有

sentences.en: some specific associations like associating red with joy and amusement and more positive associations.
sentences.zh: 一些特定的联结，比如将红色与喜悦、娱乐以及更多积极的情感联系起来。

sentences.en: So, kind of our culture is shaping the universally-based color motion associations.
sentences.zh: 所以，某种程度上我们的文化正在塑造基于普遍性的色彩情感联结。

sentences.en: And is that intrinsic or is it somehow learned?
sentences.zh: 这是天生的，还是某种程度上后天习得的？

sentences.en: Because many of us are just exposed to these kinds of concepts.
sentences.zh: 因为我们许多人都只是接触过这类概念。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, it's not an easy question to answer because to know that we would have to look at infants and they don't really have the language for colors and their language for emotions.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不是一个容易回答的问题，因为要搞清楚这一点，我们必须观察婴儿，而他们实际上还没有掌握颜色的语言和情感的语言。

sentences.en: So what we see in infant studies is that there is an immediate reaction to color red.
sentences.zh: 所以在婴儿研究中我们看到的是，对红色有一种即时反应。

sentences.en: So color red attracts attention and infants look at it longer and we can assume that they prefer this color.
sentences.zh: 所以红色会吸引注意力，婴儿看它的时间更长，我们可以假设他们更喜欢这种颜色。

sentences.en: But does it mean that they associate with emotions?
sentences.zh: 但这是否意味着他们将它与情感联系起来？

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: And when we go to older participants, we start seeing that these associations are emerging as children are growing up and the older children get, the more diverse associations get,
sentences.zh: 而当我们观察年龄较大的参与者时，我们开始看到随着孩子长大，这些联结正在出现，而且孩子们越大，联结就越多样化，

sentences.en: which is kind of showing that they are learning it over time by being in society.
sentences.zh: 这某种程度上表明他们是通过身处社会而随着时间推移学习到这一点的。

sentences.en: And in fact, here fits in the research I'm currently conducting on blind participants, that even if people who have never seen color in their life, so they are blind from birth,
sentences.zh: 事实上，这与我目前正在进行的关于盲人参与者的研究不谋而合。即使是那些生来失明、一生中从未见过颜色的人，

sentences.en: they can still associate colors with emotions in a very similar way.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然可以用非常相似的方式将颜色与情感联系起来。

sentences.en: So again, we're talking about this universality, and we're talking about the idea that color-emotion associations are learned.
sentences.zh: 所以再次说明，我们谈论的是这种普遍性，我们也谈论的是色彩情感联结是后天习得的这种观点。

sentences.en: I mentioned in the introduction some color phrases like feeling blue when you're sad or being green with envy.
sentences.zh: 我在引言中提到了一些颜色短语，比如悲伤时感到忧郁（feeling blue），或是嫉妒得发绿（green with envy）。

sentences.en: Do you have any favorite color metaphors from other languages or cultures that maybe would surprise English speakers?
sentences.zh: 你有没有什么来自其他语言或文化的、可能会让英语使用者感到惊奇的最喜欢的颜色隐喻？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, I wanted to comment on this feeling blue, because this is the metaphor that only exists in English.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我想评论一下这个“feeling blue（感到忧郁）”，因为这是一个只存在于英语中的隐喻。

sentences.en: So when we go to other languages, we don't find it.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们转向其他语言时，我们找不到它。

sentences.en: And we find that people think blue is a very positive color associated with calmness, contentment, relaxation.
sentences.zh: 我们发现人们认为蓝色是一个非常积极的颜色，与平静、满足、放松联系在一起，

sentences.en: and even english speakers in addition to associating blue with sadness they are associating
sentences.zh: 而且英语使用者除了将蓝色与悲伤联系在一起之外，他们也正在将

sentences.en: it with positive emotions now um talking about color metaphors in other languages as we know
sentences.zh: 它与积极的情感联系起来。现在，嗯，说到其他语言中的颜色隐喻，众所周知，

sentences.en: metaphors are notoriously difficult to translate but maybe i can mention one from my native
sentences.zh: 隐喻是出了名的难翻译，但也许我可以提一个来自我的母语

sentences.en: language language lithuanian where we um talking about the degrees of anger through different colors
sentences.zh: 立陶宛语的例子，我们在其中嗯通过不同的颜色来谈论愤怒的程度，

sentences.en: so if you are a little bit angry um you are white and then you get a little you get more angry than you are red.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一点点生气，嗯，你是白色的；然后你变得更生气一点，然后你是红色的。

sentences.en: I think that's like the standard anger.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就像是标准的愤怒。

sentences.en: And then you get furious, you get black.
sentences.zh: 然后你变得狂怒，你是黑色的。

sentences.en: And if you are extremely, extremely furious, then you are purple.
sentences.zh: 如果你极其、极其狂怒，那么你是紫色的。

sentences.en: So languages can also code not only the emotions with colors, but also the intensity of emotion with colors.
sentences.zh: 所以语言不仅可以通过颜色来编码情感，还可以通过颜色来编码情感的强度。

sentences.en: Can colors make us feel emotions?
sentences.zh: 颜色能让我们感受到情感吗？

sentences.en: Like I'm wondering if you're in a red room, are you more likely to become angry or feel amorous?
sentences.zh: 比如我在想，如果你在一个红色的房间里，你是否更容易生气或感到多情？

sentences.en: Or do you feel calmer if you're looking it blue or green in a landscape?
sentences.zh: 或者如果你看着风景中的蓝色或绿色，你会感到更平静吗？

sentences.en: This is a very good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: I've been working on the links between colors and emotions for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 我研究颜色和情感之间的联系已经10年了。

sentences.en: And every time we are researching them, we are just associating the actual, the color with the word of emotion.
sentences.zh: 每次我们研究它们时，我们其实只是将现实中的颜色与情感的词汇联系起来。

sentences.en: So it doesn't mean, this kind of research doesn't mean that colors make you feel anything.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不意味着，这种研究并不意味着颜色会让你感受到任何东西。

sentences.en: To answer this question, we have to put people in spaces that are colored through let's say vr or light or paint and then we need to
sentences.zh: 为了回答这个问题，我们必须把人放在通过比方说VR、光线或油漆着色的空间里，然后我们需要

sentences.en: measure their felt emotions so there are very few controlled studies in this domain and the ones that
sentences.zh: 测量他们感受到的情感，所以在这个领域受控的研究非常少，而现有的那些

sentences.en: are there they are showing very contradictory results so in fact it seems that colors are not affecting our emotions that much especially they're not affecting them so specifically
sentences.zh: 研究显示出非常矛盾的结果，事实上，似乎颜色并没有那么大程度地影响我们的情感，尤其是它们没有产生那么具体的影响，

sentences.en: that if you are in a red room you would feel anger yes maybe you feel a little bit more excited
sentences.zh: 以至于如果你在一个红色的房间里，你就会感到愤怒，是的，也许你感觉稍微有点兴奋，

sentences.en: That's one of the findings that we have.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的发现之一。

sentences.en: Red increases arousal, but somewhat.
sentences.zh: 红色会增加唤醒度，但在某种程度上。

sentences.en: But the effects of colors on emotions are not so specific.
sentences.zh: 但颜色对情感的影响并不是那么具体。

sentences.en: So when we talk about all these links, like yellow and joy, or envy and green, we are really in the domain of our minds.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们谈论所有这些联系时，比如黄色和喜悦，或者嫉妒和绿色，我们实际上是在我们思维的领域里。

sentences.en: We're not really in the domain of felt emotions.
sentences.zh: 我们其实不在所感受到的情感的领域里。

sentences.en: So in prepping for this, I ran into some stories about the idea of drunk tank pink.
sentences.zh: 所以为了做准备，我偶然看到了一些关于“囚室粉”（drunk tank pink）概念的故事。

sentences.en: And I'm hoping that you have encountered that in your work as well.
sentences.zh: 我希望你在工作中也遇到过这种情况。

sentences.en: This came from some research years ago that led to some prisons painting cells, a particular shade of pink, thinking that it was going to calm down the inmates.
sentences.zh: 这来自于多年前的一些研究，导致一些监狱把牢房漆成特定的粉红色，认为这会使囚犯冷静下来。

sentences.en: But then later they discovered this was flawed.
sentences.zh: 但后来他们发现这是有缺陷的。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that research and what's wrong with it?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈那项研究以及它有什么问题吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so you're talking about the Baker-Miller thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以你指的是贝克-米勒粉（Baker-Miller pink）。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, the Baker-Miller thing.
sentences.zh: 对，贝克-米勒粉。

sentences.en: And so the original studies were conducted in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 所以最初的研究是在70年代进行的。

sentences.en: And they showed that prisoners supposedly got karma when they were in the pink space.
sentences.zh: 它们表明，当囚犯处于粉红色的空间时，他们据称变得更平静了。

sentences.en: But in fact, they didn't really run the studies the way we are running studies nowadays.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，他们并没有真正按照我们现在进行研究的方式来进行研究。

sentences.en: In other words, the prisoners spent one year in the white cells and then the second year in the pink cells.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，囚犯在白色牢房里度过了一年，然后在粉红色牢房里度过了第二年。

sentences.en: So obviously, when you spend longer in the cells, you are less aggressive.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，当你在牢房里待的时间更长时，你的攻击性就会降低。

sentences.en: And in 2015, Gensho and colleagues re-ran the study in using modern methods in psychological science.
sentences.zh: 而在2015年，根肖（Gensho）及其同事使用心理学科学中的现代方法重新进行了这项研究。

sentences.en: And they found absolutely no difference between the white and the pink rooms for prisoners' aggressiveness.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，对于囚犯的攻击性而言，白色房间和粉红色房间之间绝对没有区别。

sentences.en: So we can say that no, Baker Miller Pink is not reducing aggressiveness in prisoners.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以说，不，贝克-米勒粉并没有减少囚犯的攻击性。

sentences.en: And yet today, one in five prisons in Europe have at least one pink prison cell.
sentences.zh: 然而今天，欧洲五分之一的监狱至少有一个粉红色的牢房。

sentences.en: So what does it mean?
sentences.zh: 这说明了什么？

sentences.en: We are implementing the findings that we are not sure about much faster than the science can run behind.
sentences.zh: 我们实施那些我们并不确定的研究结果的速度，要比科学跟进的速度快得多。

sentences.en: And therefore, it's so important to run systematic studies and really understand the phenomenon before we are bringing them into our consumers, our policymakers.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们向消费者和政策制定者推出它们之前，进行系统性的研究并真正理解这一现象是多么重要啊。

sentences.en: acres.
sentences.zh: acres。

sentences.en: So, speaking of controversial studies, you've done some work in the area of chromotherapy,
sentences.zh: 所以，说到有争议的研究，你在色彩疗法（chromotherapy）领域做过一些工作，

sentences.en: which purports to show that certain colors might have healing properties.
sentences.zh: 该疗法声称某些颜色可能具有治疗特性。

sentences.en: Is there any scientific evidence to support that notion?

sentences.en: A short answer is no, not yet.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是：没有，还没有。

sentences.en: So, I will tell you quickly about the study we conducted.
sentences.zh: 所以，我将快速向你介绍我们进行的研究。

sentences.zh: 一半的参与者看到了颜色，另一半的参与者看到了一张白色的纸，

sentences.zh: 方面，比如音乐和引导式呼吸，我们发现

sentences.zh: 干预后的压力和焦虑比干预前有所减少，所以这

sentences.en: speaks as if the intervention worked the problem was that this reduction was exactly the same for
sentences.zh: 说明干预起作用了。问题在于，这种减少对于

sentences.zh: 看颜色的组和看白纸的组来说是完全一样的，

sentences.en: so it means that it's not really due to color but probably other aspects i mean we know that
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着这其实不是由于颜色，而可能是其他方面。我的意思是，我们知道

sentences.en: mindfulness works meditation works so we just proved kind of the same thing but when it comes
sentences.zh: 正念有效，冥想有效，我们只是证明了某种相同的事情。但当谈到

sentences.zh: 而那些处于颜色条件下的参与者则说：“哦，你知道的，我闭上眼睛，只是在听
